key_insight: The paper introduces a unified operational framework to quantify and bound temporal, spatial, and total spatiotemporal correlations in quantum noise by measuring optimal distinguishability from idealized free-process classes.
engineering_relevance: It gives hardware teams practical correlation metrics and dimension-based bounds that can certify memory size, detect nonclassical noise, and flag model mismatches in quantum devices.
method: Uses process tensors to define correlation measures for temporal, spatial, and combined noise.
Optimizes distinguishability over admissible probing combs to ensure monotonicity under free-preserving superprocesses.
Derives accessible lower bounds via Choi-state functionals and restricted probes, plus dimension-dependent upper bounds on memory-transmitted temporal correlations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports effective superconducting-qubit models with ZZ and XY interactions that saturate the classical-memory, quantum-memory, and system-dimension ceilings.
watch_item: Certified lower bounds depend on probe choice and model assumptions, so incomplete probing could underestimate correlations or misidentify the true memory class.
paper_title: Quantifying and Bounding Spatiotemporal Correlations in Quantum Noise
